title: Rabbi Abbahu (Yuchasin Notice)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Yuchasin cites “Rav Ada and Rava bar Chanan came to him” in chapter Makom SheNahagu. Seder HaDorot writes: “I have not found it.” It occurs in Pesachim 51a in the Dikdukei Soferim reading. The Rif reads “they came and said to Abbahu”; Yuchasin read “to Rabbi Abbahu.” The Rif and Ran reading “to Shmuel’s father” is a printing error. The correct reading must be Rav Avya Saba (Rav Huna’s student, as in Beitzah 21a) and Rabbah bar Rav Huna came and spoke to “his father,” meaning Rav Huna.

notes.text: Hyman’s proposed reading separates “his father” from the personal name Abbahu and identifies the father as Rav Huna. It remains his emendation.

The consulted Davidson Pesachim 51a names Rav Avira Saba and Rabbah son of Rav Huna, who report to Abaye, in the account of Rabbah bar bar Chana. This differs from Hyman’s reported Abbahu, father-of-Shmuel and his-father readings. His proposed Avya/Rav Huna reconstruction and printing-error diagnosis remain his argument; the exact Rif, Ran, Yuchasin and Dikdukei Soferim readings have not been independently inspected.
